item.title: Prop-WRF: Proposal-Guided Wireless Radiance Field for Scalable Multi-Frequency Outdoor Channel Frequency Response Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.11845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse-directional wireless radiance fields (WRFs) enable complex channel frequency response (CFR) prediction from receiver locations and multipath direction priors. However, in large-scale outdoor environments, long sampling intervals make it difficult to concentrate a limited sampling budget around valid virtual anchors (VAs), degrading prediction accuracy and training stability. This paper proposes Prop-WRF, a proposalnetwork-guided WRF for CFR prediction across multiple subcarriers. A lightweight proposal network learns VA occupancy densities through online distillation from the main network and iteratively guides resampling toward likely VA locations. The main network then predicts complex radiance over the refined intervals and synthesizes CFRs using an analytical propagation model. By introducing frequency encoding only into the radiance branch, a single model jointly learns shared VA geometry from observations across subcarriers while representing frequencydependent complex radiance. A stage-wise hybrid normalized loss and an interval-weight regularizer further strengthen weakchannel supervision and suppress spurious VA peaks. In addition, a multipath simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) front end refines receiver states and path associations to construct geometrically consistent training priors. Simulations show that Prop-WRF improves CFR prediction accuracy and training stability over conventional sparse-directional WRF baselines in larger environments.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Fu, Jiancun Fan, Shiyu Zhai, Zhibo Duan, Jie Luo

item.title: Integrating Deep PPG Representations and Digital Biomarkers for Aortic Stenosis Detection with Peri-TAVI Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2611.11871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Access to echocardiography is often limited, delaying recognition of progressive aortic stenosis (AS). A brief, low-cost physiological measurement obtained during routine care could help identify patients who may warrant earlier imaging. Here, we present PulseAS, integrating deep photoplethysmography (PPG) representations, waveform biomarkers and clinical information for high-grade AS screening. Three complementary analyses assessed (1) validation and transfer across cohorts differing in geography and ethnic composition, (2) score-based enrichment of AS and pre-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) cases, and (3) preoperative and postoperative pulse changes. Using 15-s recordings, separate patient-level cross-validation in EDU (n = 1,209) and MIMIC-III (n = 2,970) yielded AUROCs of 0.818 (PulseAS-XGB) and 0.838 (PulseAS-L2), respectively. In external validation from MIMIC-III to EDU, PulseAS-XGB achieved an AUROC of 0.716, improving to 0.813 after local adaptation. The highest-scoring 10% captured 45.2% of all high-grade AS cases in EDU and 41.3% in MIMIC-III, and 56.9% of pre-TAVI cases in EDU. Notably, in the EDU TAVI subgroup, PPG waveforms showed earlier systolic peaks and narrower systolic contours following intervention. These findings support clinical-PPG risk stratification in new populations and warrant prospective evaluation of echocardiographic prioritisation.
item.dc:creator: Haowan Wang, Cheng Ding, Donglin Xie, Huizi Yu, Guangkun Nie, Shenda Hong, Bryan P Yan, Kent Chak-yu So

item.title: Capture-Aware Predictive OFDM Reacquisition in Clock-Asynchronous Space-Air-Ground Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.11904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reacquisition must validate an intended burst and return its delay and carrier frequency offset (CFO) correc- tions within capture tolerances. In clock-asynchronous space- air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), shared geometry and timing uncertainty couples distributed observations, while public- preamble replay creates competing peaks. We propose Capture- Aware Predictive Reacquisition (CAPR), a Bayesian receiver that models competition under both hypotheses and marginalizes unknown spatial interference covariance and target complex amplitude before shared-state fusion. CAPR maximizes posterior probability mass within the capture rectangle and constrains continuous L-BFGS-B refinement through a mass-loss budget. We derive closed-form predictive likelihood reductions, an exact finite-cell action optimizer, a conditional approximation regret bound, and finite-sample false-acceptance calibration. Across 150 primary scenarios and five seeds, CAPR achieves 83.8% strict capture at 4.68% realized false acceptance, improving over Gaussian joint-MAP by 12.5 percentage points overall and 54.2 points across all 32 replay scenarios. Diffuse multipath, degraded assistance, and indistinguishable sources delineate its operational boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Zhihan Zeng, Kaihe Wang, Zhongpei Zhang, Chongwen Huang

item.title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.11956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.
item.dc:creator: Akanksha Sneh, Krishna Ayyagari, Vivaswan Nawani, Shobha Sundar Ram

item.title: Near-Field Channel Estimation via Deep Unfolding for Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.12021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Extremely Large-scale Antenna Array (ELAA) has been envisioned as a promising candidate to meet the ambitious demands of 6G. However, this evolution also brings about two primary limitations: high computational complexity caused by large-scale arrays and inherent operation in the near-field region. To address these issues, this work exploits the sparsity of near-field channels in the polar domain and formulates channel estimation as a compressed sensing (CS) problem, thereby enabling estimation with reduced pilot overhead. In particular, we propose a guideline to design a sparsifying codebook for the near-field channel, which is strictly based on a target coherence value. Building on this, we develop a deep unfolding architecture, derived from the iterative solver ISTA, with a hybrid loss, namely Hybrid LISTA. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed codebook, with comparable complexity, still exhibits improved estimation performance and greater coverage in the near-field region. Moreover, our unfolded model with the hybrid loss consistently delivers better recovery performance over existing estimation schemes.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen The Khang, Do Hai Son, Tran Trong Duy, Trung Thanh Le, Viet-Dung Nguyen, Trong-Minh Hoang, Karim Abed-Meraim, Merouane Debbah, Nguyen Linh Trung

item.title: Prospective Importance-based Cognitive Pilot Design for Semantic Sensing in ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semantic sensing enables integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to acquire environmental information relevant to downstream tasks. However, existing pilot design methods either rely on static pilot configurations or learn end-to-end pilot selection policies, without explicitly evaluating the semantic contribution of candidate pilot locations. In this work, we propose a cognitive semantic sensing framework for human activity recognition in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-ISAC systems. Rather than directly learning a high-dimensional mapping from observations to pilot locations, we introduce a semantic importance weight (SIW) to measure the semantic contribution of each candidate pilot location. Leveraging the information bottleneck (IB) principle and the mutual information-minimum mean-square error (I-MMSE) relationship, SIW assigns high values to future time-frequency (TF) channel coefficients that are both difficult to infer from the preceding observations and valuable for downstream inference. To efficiently obtain the SIW, we further develop a conditional diffusion model that predicts the corresponding uncertainty through denoising covariance estimation. Experiments on a real-world Wi-Fi sensing dataset show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baselines across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and pilot budgets.
item.dc:creator: Guanping Shang, Anzheng Tang, Zeyan Zhuang, Shenghui Song

item.title: Joint Power and Adaptive-Constellation Optimization for OFDM-ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12166v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Next-generation wireless systems are expected to support integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). However, sensing imposes different requirements on the power allocation (PA) and the modulation format than communications, leading to a fundamental trade-off in frequency-selective channels. In this paper, we jointly optimize the PA and modulation format for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM)-based ISAC systems, considering both target detection and tracking. We first derive an upper bound on the mutual information to predict the communication performance for power-constellation allocation. We then use an autoencoder (AE) to learn a family of finite constellations that realizes the allocation under different sensing constraints without retraining. The results show that tracking alleviates the sensing & communications (S&C) tradeoff compared with initial detection, and that the PA and the modulation dominate the S&C trade-off at low and high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), respectively. At intermediate SNR, the proposed joint optimization significantly outperforms individual optimizations, while the pretrained adaptive constellation family almost fully realizes the predicted allocation gains.
item.dc:creator: Benedikt Geiger, Linus Hampel, Laurent Schmalen

item.title: Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.12250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (named Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple aerial wardens that attempt to detect the transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of warden channel state information (CSI), we develop a unified robust covert transmission framework that incorporates bounded and statistical CSI error models. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, the artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions at Alice to maximize the minimum weighted signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among the legitimate users subject to data covertness constraints. The resulting optimization problem is intractable to solve optimally due to the strong coupling among the optimization variables and the random channel uncertainty. To deal with this issue, we propose a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based algorithm. Specifically, for the norm-bounded CSI error model, we first employ the S-procedure to convert the covertness constraints into a sequence of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Then, a successive convex approximation (SCA) procedure incorporating semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and bisection search techniques is proposed to solve the resulting problem. For the statistical CSI error model, the Bernstein-type inequality is employed to derive deterministic approximations of the probabilistic constraint in terms of LMIs and second-order cone (SOC) constraints that can be efficiently tackled. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Dong, Ran Yang, Weidong Mei, Zheng Dong, Yue Xiu, Daniel Benevides da Costa, Zhongpei Zhang, Ning We

item.title: Robust Beamforming and Antenna Position Optimization for Movable Antenna-Assisted Covert Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.12342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a movable antenna (MA)-enhanced covert communication system, where a legitimate transmitter (Alice) serves multiple legitimate users in the presence of multiple non-colluding Willies that attempt to detect the covert transmission from Alice. To ensure data covertness with imperfect knowledge of the Willies' channel state information (CSI), we develop a robust covert transmission framework with a norm-bounded CSI error model. In particular, we aim to jointly optimize the transmit beamforming vectors, artificial noise (AN) covariance matrix, and MA positions to maximize the weighted minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among all legitimate users subject to worst-case covertness constraints. To tackle this challenging problem, we develop a block coordinate descent (BCD)-based optimization framework, incorporating the S-procedure, semidefinite relaxation (SDR), bisection search, and successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of MA-enhanced covert communication systems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Dong, Ran Yang, Weidong Mei, Zheng Dong, Yue Xiu, Zhongpei Zhang, Tony Q. S. Quek

item.title: Neural Multipath Fields for 6G FR3 Digital Twins: Latent Adaptation from Sparse Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.12425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless digital twins are essential for environment-aware 6G communications, motivating the investigation of frequency range 3 (FR3), an emerging mid-band regime offering a promising balance between bandwidth and propagation characteristics. Neural Radio Frequency (RF) fields provide continuous surrogates for site-specific radio propagation, but adapting a scene-specific field to a new environment can require substantial measurements and retraining. To this end, we propose the Latent-Adaptive Neural Multipath Field (LANMF), a scene-conditioned FR3 model that predicts path-resolved delays, complex channel impulse response (CIR) coefficients, and arrival and departure directions from transmitter-receiver coordinates. LANMF learns shared propagation representations across source environments and adapts to unseen scenes by optimizing only a 16-dimensional scene latent. Evaluated on six ray-traced indoor scenes at 7.5 GHz, latent-only adaptation yields improvements in prediction with just 5-10 target links (0.42-0.83% of available links). Compared with full-network fine-tuning, it updates only 16 persistent target parameters, reducing adaptation time by 28-30% and incremental peak GPU memory by 82-85%. While the proposed solution supports various wireless applications, we demonstrate its utility through beam-candidate reduction using a 64-beam codebook, retaining measurement-based final beam selection.
item.dc:creator: Srijita Sanyal, Adam Umra, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Grid Design for Near-Field Channel Estimation with Uniform Linear Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.12457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops deterministic grids for line-of-sight near-field channel estimation with uniform linear arrays (ULAs) and hybrid receivers. A normalized channel approximation squared error (NCASE) criterion leads to geometric covering problems under a constant-amplitude parabolic model and an elliptical approximation of the correlation regions. For a horizontal ULA, transformation and scaling yield a disk-covering problem, addressed by adapting a hexagonal lattice to the mapped ground-plane region. For a vertical ULA, a reciprocal-distance interval cover is solved optimally by a farthest-reaching greedy procedure. Numerical evaluation with exact spherical-wave channels yields empirical maximum approximation errors close to the target and improved P-SOMP estimation relative to the tested polar-domain grids of comparable size.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Alberto D'Amico, Luca Antonelli

item.title: Coexistence of Direct-to-Device (D2D) Satellite Systems with 5G/6G Terrestrial Networks: Cross-Border Aggregate Interference Analysis in Saudi Arabia
item.description: arXiv:2611.12644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct-to-device (D2D) satellite systems, particularly those based on 3GPP-compliant non-terrestrial networks (NTN), deliver connectivity to standard mobile phones and IoT devices using terrestrial International Mobile Telecommunications (IMT) spectrum. This raises the risk of harmful cross-border interference into incumbent terrestrial IMT networks, an issue considered under Agenda Item 1.13 of the ITU World Radiocommunication Conference 2027 (WRC-27). This paper presents an ITU-R-compliant assessment of aggregate downlink interference from two hypothetical D2D systems operating in Jordan and Iraq into terrestrial IMT user equipment (UE) in Saudi Arabia, operating in the 698-960 MHz band. Unlike prior studies that evaluate a few test points near a simplified ideal tri-border intersection, we distribute multiple victim UEs along realistic national borders within various strips at a distance of 0-40 km from the borders. We compare two satellite selection strategies: highest-elevation and random strategies. The CDF of the interference-to-noise ratio (I/N) together with the intra-system and inter-system aggregation factors are analyzed. Results show that the protection criterion is exceeded up to 88% of the time, requiring up to 27 dB of additional isolation, so coexistence is infeasible without interference mitigation. In general, random selection produces higher interference because low-elevation beams place victims closer to boresight. Two mitigation techniques are then evaluated. A border isolation zone of one cell diameter yields only a moderate improvement under both strategies, whereas a narrow-beam, deep-null phased-array pattern lowers the exceedance to about 40% irrespective of strategy, providing an important input for spectrum regulatory considerations.
item.dc:creator: Muneer M. Alzubi, Muhammad Alrabeiah, Khalid Aldubaikhy, Abdullah Alqasir, Majed Alsifaee, Mohamed-Slim Alouini

item.title: Bayes-Optimal Quantum Computational Sensing via Convex Spectral Design
item.description: arXiv:2611.10146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum computational sensing performs task-specific inference directly through coherent sensing dynamics, avoiding an intermediate estimation step. Existing designs, however, typically optimize quantum control parameters through nonconvex programs whose performance can depend strongly on initialization. This contribution formulates binary phase classification directly in terms of the sensor's measurement response. For a fixed query budget, generalized quantum signal processing (GQSP) restricts this response to a bounded trigonometric polynomial, while the Bayes classification error is linear in the response. These properties yield an exact finite-dimensional semidefinite program for the globally Bayes-optimal sensor response. Fej\'er--Riesz factorization and GQSP synthesis then recover a physically realizable control sequence. The same formulation extends naturally to sample-based design and additive phase uncertainty. Numerical tests show improved accuracy and optimization reliability over direct control-angle training; noise-aware redesign also lowers error under phase uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Amirhossein Taherpour, Alireza Sadeghi, Georgios B. Giannakis

item.title: Receiver-Resolution APS-PDP Maps for Wireless Channels: Benchmarking and Coarse-to-Fine Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.10581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Angle Power Spectrum (APS) and Power Delay Profile (PDP) are receiver-facing spectra that govern beam selection and wideband equalization. Most ray-tracing benchmarks provide supervision as variable-size multipath component lists. This format does not match practical receivers, whose angular and delay resolutions are limited by array aperture and system bandwidth. As a result, learning targets are ambiguous and evaluations can change with reconstruction conventions. We introduce UrbanADPSMap, a benchmark that converts ray-traced supervision into fixed-grid APS and PDP targets by explicitly modeling bandwidth-limited and aperture-limited response kernels. By fixing the receiver-domain kernels, discretization, and validity mask, UrbanADPSMap removes reconstruction-induced target ambiguity and stabilizes downstream evaluation across methods. Built on this benchmark, we propose SpecFlowAR, a coarse-to-fine generator based on multi-scale autoregressive flow matching. The model first captures coarse dispersion structure and then refines beam-relevant peaks and low-power tails. The number of function evaluations controls the sampling budget, enabling latency and quality to be adjusted for dense spectrum queries. Experiments on the test set show that SpecFlowAR reduces BPL@5 to 2.03 dB under a unified NFE=80 budget, while improving beam utility and reducing errors of 3GPP dispersion statistics.
item.dc:creator: Peilin Zheng, Haozhe Jia, Xiucheng Wang, Wenshuo Chen, Nan Cheng

item.title: PENSA: A Spatial Accelerator for BitNet b1.58 Inference on an HBM-equipped AMD Alveo FPGA
item.description: arXiv:2611.10648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ternary large language models (tLLMs) replace general multiplication in dominant linear layers with sign-controlled accumulation, shifting hardware bottlenecks toward packed-weight delivery, reduction, and operator occupancy. PENSA is an end-to-end FPGA accelerator for the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model on an AMD Alveo U50. Two row-partitioned ternary matrix engines consume packed TQ1_0 weights from eight independent high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pseudo-channels, each processing 1,280 ternary weights per cycle through sign selection and integer reduction. The sequencer, attention, and vocabulary-projection units remain resident on the FPGA, while two-stream interleaved scheduling overlaps sequences across the persistent pipeline to form the Penta-Unit. At 104.1~MHz, PENSA achieves 58.09 tok/s at context 128 and 24.60 tok/s at context 2048, corresponding to 2.14-3.14$\times$ the throughput of a same-model Xeon E-2356G baseline. The resulting system demonstrates end-to-end FPGA execution of 2B-scale BitNet topology without modifying its model structure.
item.dc:creator: Karthikeyan B. Kalyanasundara, Ivan S. Maksymo, Philip H. W. Leong

item.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.10743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.
item.dc:creator: Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos

item.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.10952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.
item.dc:creator: Irtiza Hasan, Ahmed Arafa

item.title: CHANNELS4WORLD: An Environment-Scale Dataset for Wireless Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wireless foundation models learn reusable representations across tasks, configurations, and deployment environments. Their pretraining requires environmental breadth, yet wireless datasets often sample few sites densely. We introduce Channels4World, a scene-centered dataset of 100,000 distinct outdoor RF scenes and a procedural method for generating them. Each scene links a generated environment and RF material assignments to 32 base-station (BS) positions, 16,384 UE positions, and aligned variable-length multipath and ordered interaction records at 3.5 and 7~GHz. The corpus comprises 52.43 billion physical BS-UE pairs, 104.86 billion frequency-specific evaluations, and a 29.14-TB packaged payload. Scene identity aligns geometry, placements, channels, and interactions across frequencies, allowing environmental breadth and within-scene observation density to vary independently. The public release offers predefined subsets at multiple scales and separate access to corpus components. A deterministic 90K/10K scene-level train-test split keeps both frequencies and all scene components together. We characterize morphology, RF materials, and transceiver placement across three generation profiles. Controlled propagation and path-retention analyses show that diffraction materially affects retained-link availability and multipath structure, while the retention policy reduces storage substantially with little loss in represented aggregate power. Under matched training exposure, models trained on broader scene collections perform better on held-out scenes, although an equal-episode control shows that scene count alone cannot explain the gain. By making environmental breadth explicit and controllable, Channels4World supports the development and evaluation of wireless foundation models for generalization across deployment environments.
item.dc:creator: Joonkyu Jang, Hyung-Joo Moon, Kwang Soon Kim, Seong-Lyun Kim, Jakob Hoydis, Robert W. Heath, Jr., Chan-Byoung Chae

item.title: Joint LSFC and Nakagami-m Estimation From Downlink SINR in GZF-Precoded CF-mMIMO
item.description: arXiv:2611.11849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate characterization of the instantaneous signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) is important for reliability-sensitive cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems. This paper proposes a joint estimation method for link-specific large-scale fading coefficients (LSFCs) and a common Nakagami-$m$ shape parameter using power and downlink SINR measurements. A tractable SINR distribution is first derived under global zero-forcing (GZF) precoding, Nakagami-$m$ fading, and link-level fractional power control (FPC). Based on the derived probability density function (PDF), a model-driven neural network (NN) is developed to solve the resulting maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) problem. Simulations show that the reconstructed SINR distributions obtained with the estimated parameters closely match the empirical distributions. With $2 \times 10^{5}$ samples, the proposed method achieves an LSFC root-mean-square error (RMSE) of approximately 1.0 dB and an $m$ RMSE of approximately 0.085.
item.dc:creator: Longfei Liu, Yichen Guo, Lili Xu, Yihang Cheng, Tao Peng, Wenbo Wang

item.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
item.description: arXiv:2611.11872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.
item.dc:creator: Nir Sharon, Sheng Xu

item.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.11951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.
item.dc:creator: Yue Wang, Haoxin Chen, Xiaoqing Guo

item.title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG
item.description: arXiv:2611.12026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Typical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) occurs only after significant dopaminergic loss, while resting-state EEG abnormalities like alpha slowing and reduced coherence occur earlier. While many published EEG-based PD detectors claim accuracy greater than 95%, many use epoch-level splits which leak subject identity. I introduce MambaPD, a bidirectional selective state space model for resting-state EEG-based PD detection, blending the channel mixing, patch tokenization and bidirectional Mamba encoder. It is compared with four baselines (TCN, BiLSTM with attention, EEGNet and a patch Transformer) in two public datasets (UNM, SanDiego) using subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation (checkpoints were selected on the held-out fold, so absolute estimates are optimistic). On UNM the accuracy is between 0.67 and 0.71, and MambaPD (0.714) is not statistically distinguishable from the Transformer (0.715), and TCN (0.708), with the highest sensitivity (0.82), while the lowest specificity (0.52). For the smaller SanDiego cohort, accuracy is in the range of 0.60 to 0.70, with the highest scores (0.703) from TCN and the lowest (0.601) from EEGNet, while MambaPD scores 0.631, with the lowest specificity (0.46) among the five models. The differences among the models on UNM are minor compared to the differences among folds. I report the whole pipeline, per-fold results, and the shortcomings of the protocol.
item.dc:creator: Ayesha Zulfiqar

item.title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
item.description: arXiv:2611.12036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.
item.dc:creator: Akihito Noda, Ryo Takahashi

item.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
item.description: arXiv:2611.12223v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Studer

item.title: A Scale-Space Theory of Memory
item.description: arXiv:2611.12316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scale-space theory has emerged as a central attempt to restrict the {\it general} theory of signal processing with geometric constraints inspired from the animal world. In the mathematical language of operator theory, scale-space theory restricts the Toeplitz operator. The present paper investigates scale-space theory for memory systems. We investigate how scale space theory restricts a memory system encoding past information, that is, restricts the Hankel operator. Our main result is to establish a close correspondence between scale-space theory and the long-studied {\it relaxation} property.
item.dc:creator: Dongjun Wu, Rodolphe Sepulchre

item.title: VNA-Only Calibration of Waveguide Thermistor Mounts with Self-Consistent Determination of the Thermistor-Port Impedance
item.description: arXiv:2611.12369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A method is presented for determining the calibration factor and the effective efficiency of waveguide thermistor mounts from vector-network-analyzer reflection data alone, without a microcalorimeter, extending the three reflection-coefficient method of the coaxial case. In waveguide the thermistor is coupled to the line through a matching structure and the reference impedance of the thermistor port, $Z_0$, is not known a priori; it is inferred through a power-consistency relation between pairs of states, under the convention that it is real. The method reproduces the factory certificates (U = 2 %) of four K486A mounts within 1.0 % rms and the PTB-traceable values (U = 0.85 to 0.98 %) of a fifth within 0.34 % rms; its expanded measurement uncertainty is 0.5 to 1.16 % (k = 2) for the best specimen and below 2 % for the five. A mount with its waveguide-to-coaxial adapter is calibrated directly, without characterizing the adapter, from the model factor of the mount and the geometric factor measured through the adapter. The scattering matrix implied by the solution is not passive; a minimum-norm correction of the thermistor impedances along the two directions invisible to the calibration factor - the ratios of the efficiencies of the three states - brings it to the floor of passivity, where the efficiency depends on the load only through its mismatch factor, leaves the result unchanged, and gives the sensitivity of the efficiency to the bias resistance in closed form: below $4\times10^{-5}$ $\Omega^{-1}$ in band mean, proportional to the mismatch of the operating state and to the loss of the mount.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Greco

item.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.12480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $\alpha$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/\lambda)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/\epsilon^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.
item.dc:creator: Symeon Vaidanis, Photios A. Stavrou, Marios Kountouris

item.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.12527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. Unlike recent TTS pipelines, WaveGen does not rely on separately trained or externally decoded intermediate representations, such as neural audio codecs, Mel-spectrogram vocoders, or VAE-based latent models. In addition, WaveGen performs internal text-speech alignment within a single model, eliminating the need for external alignment modules such as duration predictors. To preserve a truly end-to-end formulation, our framework further avoids dependence on self-supervised representations, such as BERT-based text embeddings and Wav2Vec 2.0-based semantic representations, as well as semantic distillation methods for training optimization. To achieve this, we carefully design Spectral Forcing, a model architecture with disentangled diffusion heads, and a training objective based on a multi-scale spectral $v$-loss. We further validate the scalability of end-to-end TTS models by scaling the model size from 0.1B to 0.6B parameters. Using a single architecture, open-source data, and one-stage training, without external modules such as duration predictor or REPA, WaveGen demonstrates fully end-to-end waveform generation achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Emilia training dataset. In particular, WaveGen achieves a WER of 1.47 and a SIM of 0.75 on the Seed-en benchmark. Source code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/sh-lee-prml/WaveGen
item.dc:creator: Sang-Hoon Lee, Ha-Yeong Choi

item.title: Deep learning for structural health monitoring: An application to heritage structures
item.description: arXiv:2211.10351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thanks to recent advancements in numerical methods, computer power, and monitoring technology, seismic ambient noise provides precious information about the structural behavior of old buildings. The measurement of the vibrations produced by anthropic and environmental sources and their use for dynamic identification and structural health monitoring of buildings initiated an emerging, cross-disciplinary field engaging seismologists, engineers, mathematicians, and computer scientists. In this work, we employ recent deep learning techniques for time-series forecasting to inspect and detect anomalies in the large dataset recorded during a long-term monitoring campaign conducted on the San Frediano bell tower in Lucca. We frame the problem as an unsupervised anomaly detection task and train a Temporal Fusion Transformer to learn the normal dynamics of the structure. We then detect the anomalies by looking at the differences between the predicted and observed frequencies.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Carrara, Fabrizio Falchi, Maria Girardi, Nicola Messina, Cristina Padovani, Daniele Pellegrini

item.title: Image Steganography For Securing Intellicise Wireless Networks: "Invisible Encryption" Against Eavesdroppers
item.description: arXiv:2505.04467v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As one of the most promising technologies for intellicise (intelligent and consice) wireless networks, Semantic Communication (SemCom) significantly improves communication efficiency by extracting, transmitting, and recovering semantic information, while reducing transmission delay. However, an integration of communication and artificial intelligence (AI) also exposes SemCom to security and privacy threats posed by intelligent eavesdroppers. To address this challenge, image steganography in SemCom embeds secret semantic features within cover semantic features, allowing intelligent eavesdroppers to decode only the cover image. This technique offers a form of "invisible encryption" for SemCom. Motivated by these advancements, this paper conducts a comprehensive exploration of integrating image steganography into SemCom. Firstly, we assess the potential of image steganography in enhancing the security of SemCom. Secondly, we delve into traditional and DL-based image steganographic paradigms for securing SemCom. Thirdly, we further discuss six image semantic steganography strategies. Fourthly, we present a case study to illustrate the effectiveness of coverless steganography SemCom. Finally, we propose future research directions for image steganography SemCom.
item.dc:creator: Rui Meng, Song Gao, Haixiao Gao, Yinqiu Liu, Ruichen Zhang, Huishi Song, Mengying Sun, Xiaodong Xu, Ping Zhang

item.title: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2512.17473v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving nonlinear matrix decompositions (NMD). Given an input matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and a factorization rank $r \ll \min(m, n)$, NMD seeks matrices $W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ such that $X \approx f(WH)$, where $f$ is an element-wise nonlinear function. We evaluate our method on several representative nonlinear models: the rectified linear unit activation $f(x) = \max(0, x)$, suitable for nonnegative sparse data approximation, the component-wise square $f(x) = x^2$, applicable to probabilistic circuit representation, and the MinMax transform $f(x) = \min(b, \max(a, x))$, relevant for recommender systems. The proposed framework flexibly supports diverse loss functions, including least squares, $\ell_1$ norm, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and can be readily extended to other nonlinearities and metrics. We illustrate the applicability, efficiency, and adaptability of the approach on real-world datasets, highlighting its potential for a broad range of applications.
item.dc:creator: Atharva Awari, Nicolas Gillis, Arnaud Vandaele

item.title: Assessment of Errors of Fundamental Frequency Estimation Methods in the Presence of Voltage Fluctuations and Distortions
item.description: arXiv:2601.16606v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fundamental frequency is one of the parameters that define power quality. Correctly determining this parameter under the conditions that prevail in modern power grids is crucial. Diagnostic purposes often require an efficient estimation of this parameter within short time windows. Therefore, this article presents the results of numerical simulation studies that allow the assessment of errors in various fundamental frequency estimation methods, including the standard IEC 61000-4-30 method, when the analyzed signal has a form similar to that found in modern power grids. For the purposes of this study, a test signal was adopted recreating the states of the power grid, including the simultaneous occurrence of voltage fluctuations and distortions. Conclusions are presented based on conducted research.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: A. Bracale, P. De Falco, P. Kuwa{\l}ek and G. Wiczy\'nski, Assessment of Errors of Fundamental Frequency Estimation Methods in the Presence of Voltage Fluctuations and Distortions, 2026 22nd ICHQP, Dresden, Germany, 2026
item.dc:creator: Antonio Bracale, Pasquale De Falco, Piotr Kuwa{\l}ek, Grzegorz Wiczy\'nski

item.title: Beamforming Gain Maximization for Fluid Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface: A Minkowski Geometry Approach
item.description: arXiv:2602.11654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies joint beamforming and configuration optimization for a fluid reconfigurable intelligent surface (FRIS)-assisted downlink system with port selection and finite-resolution phase shifts. We develop an alternating-optimization (AO) framework that combines a closed-form maximum-ratio transmission update with a globally optimal FRIS update for a fixed beamformer, and converges monotonically within finitely many iterations. The key idea is to represent the feasible reflected-signal set as a union of Minkowski sums over port subsets and to characterize its maximum magnitude through support functions. This reduces the FRIS subproblem to a one-dimensional directional search, in which the optimal configuration is obtained by selecting the ports with the largest direction-dependent scores together with their best phase codewords. For uniformly quantized phase codebooks, closed-form scores and a finite set of critical angles are derived, identifying the global optimum with near-quadratic complexity. Numerical results demonstrate superior performance over existing benchmarks, near-optimal beamforming gains, robustness to channel uncertainty, and rapid convergence.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Bae Jeon

item.title: CRLB Minimization for Multi-Target Localization in Segmented Waveguide-Enabled Pinching-Antenna ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.00572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The segmented waveguide-enabled pinching-antenna system (SWAN) has been proposed to mitigate the inter-antenna radiation problem in uplink transmissions of conventional pinching-antenna (PA) systems. In this work, SWAN-assisted multi-user multi-target integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) is investigated, where a SWAN-enabled base station (BS) provides downlink communications for multiple communication users (CUs) and performs sensing for multiple targets. The dual-functional signals transmitted by the BS are radiated by the SWAN, and the echo signals reflected by the targets are captured by the SWAN and relayed to the BS for estimating the locations of the targets. We adopt the Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) for target location estimation as the sensing metric, and formulate a CRLB minimization problem to evaluate the performance of the ISAC system. For joint PA position and beamforming optimization, we develop a Riemannian manifold optimization (RMO) method, in which a product variable representing both the beamforming and PA position variables is constrained on a constructed Riemannian product manifold (RPM). A penalty method with Riemannian Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (RBFGS) algorithm is then applied to update the product variable and obtain a feasible solution, enabling simultaneous and joint optimization of the variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RMO method achieves a lower CRLB than separate optimization approaches for SWAN. Compared with existing multi-waveguide PA-assisted ISAC systems, the SWAN optimized by the proposed RMO substantially reduces the required waveguide deployment length while incurring only a marginal CRLB performance loss under typical system settings.
item.dc:creator: Yue Geng, Tee Hiang Cheng, Kah Chan Teh, Zhiguo Ding

item.title: Location-Aware Performance Analysis of HAPS-RIS-Assisted Multiple-Antenna Systems with Practical RIS Impairments
item.description: arXiv:2604.25331v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-altitude platform station (HAPS)-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer a promising means of extending the coverage and reliability of future 6G and beyond wireless networks, but their performance is strongly affected by cascaded line-of-sight (LoS)-dominant fading, practical RIS hardware impairments, and location-dependent atmospheric attenuation. This paper develops a tractable performance-analysis framework for HAPS-RIS-assisted multiple-antenna systems over cascaded Rician--Rician channels. The small-scale effective channel power is statistically characterized by exploiting the structured covariance of the cascaded channel and applying saddlepoint approximation (SPA), while the composite log-normal large-scale fading and atmosphere-dependent attenuation are incorporated through Gauss-Hermite quadrature to obtain tractable approximations for the received-SNR distribution and outage probability. The framework further accounts for finite-resolution RIS phase shifts and phase-dependent reflection amplitudes. To connect the analysis with a realistic deployment, the transmitter, receiver, and HAPS locations are mapped through Earth-centered Earth-fixed east-north-up (ECEF-ENU) coordinate transformations to obtain the propagation directions and array steering vectors, enabling geometry-aided transmit precoding and LoS-aligned RIS phase configuration without requiring full instantaneous channel state information (CSI). Monte Carlo simulations show excellent agreement with the proposed analytical probability density function (PDF) and outage expressions. Moreover, the geometry-aided LoS-aligned precoder achieves outage performance nearly indistinguishable from instantaneous dominant-eigenmode precoding.
item.dc:creator: Tayfun Yilmaz, Haci Ilhan, Ali Gorcin, Halim Yanikomeroglu

item.title: The Resurrection of Spectrum Spreading for 6G and Beyond: From Sinusoids to Chirps
item.description: arXiv:2605.00249v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) and its sinusoidal subcarriers have underpinned the 4G and 5G eras, delivering high spectral efficiency and resilience to multipath fading through an efficient multicarrier architecture. However, as future systems move toward doubly dispersive environments driven by high-mobility applications and migration to mmWave/sub-THz bands, the time-invariance assumption underlying OFDM becomes increasingly difficult to maintain, and Doppler-induced degradation becomes prominent. While enhancements such as MIMO, advanced coding, and scheduling provide incremental remedies, they introduce additional overhead, because the sinusoidal subcarrier itself offers no inherent waveform-level robustness to Doppler impairments. Accordingly, two time-frequency spreading philosophies have emerged to improve Doppler resilience by distributing each symbol's energy across both dimensions of the time-frequency plane: (i) 2D isotropic spreading via the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, exemplified by the orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) family, and (ii) sheared spreading via parameterizable chirps, exemplified by the affine frequency-division multiplexing (AFDM) family. In this article, we examine key considerations for future waveform design across these paradigms and argue that transitioning from the sinusoidal subcarriers of OFDM to the chirp-based subcarriers offers a viable design direction for improving Doppler robustness while retaining much of the mature OFDM infrastructure. This perspective also highlights the suitability of chirp-based waveforms for integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) and their extensibility to emerging physical-layer techniques. Overall, we argue that the transition from sinusoids to chirps is a technically motivated, compelling evolutionary direction for future wireless physical layer design.
item.dc:creator: Hyeon Seok Rou, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu, Emil Bj\"ornson, Sunwoo Kim, Marios Kountouris

item.title: PPG2ECG: Physiology-Guided Latent Rectified Flow for Electro-Hemodynamic PPG-to-ECG Generation
item.description: arXiv:2605.12541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is the clinical standard for cardiac assessment but requires dedicated hardware that does not scale to daily-life monitoring. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is ubiquitous in wearables but lacks ECG-specific diagnostic morphology and is corrupted by motion and sensor noise. PPG-to-ECG generation aims to bridge this gap by recovering electrical morphology and timing from peripheral pulse signals. However, existing methods largely rely on statistical alignment and data-driven generation. They fail to explicitly structure the latent space around physiology-aware electro-hemodynamic factors and lack constraints from forward physiological dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose PPG2ECG, a physiology-guided latent rectified flow framework. PPG2ECG introduces an electro-hemodynamic simulator that co-models ECG and PPG through shared cardiac phase dynamics. Guided by this simulator, a Physiology-Aware AutoEncoder learns a structured electro-hemodynamic latent space. Then we integrate this simulator guidance into a PPG-conditioned latent rectified flow, enforcing ECG-side morphology consistency and ECG-to-PPG forward hemodynamic consistency during generative transport. Experiments on the large-scale MC-MED dataset demonstrate that PPG2ECG significantly improves PPG-to-ECG generation and downstream cardiovascular disease classification, proving its ability to generate ECGs that are both signal-faithful and physiologically plausible under the ECG-to-PPG hemodynamic pathway
item.dc:creator: Xiaoda Wang, Minxiao Wang, Kaiqiao Han, Defu Cao, Ching Chang, Yidan Shi, Runze Yan, Xiao Luo, Yan Liu, Xiao Hu, Yizhou Sun, Wei Wang, Carl Yang

item.title: Near-Field Communications with Different Array Geometries: Rayleigh Distance, Channel Estimation, and Transmission Design
item.description: arXiv:2605.17690v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work establishes a framework of near-field communication under different array geometries of extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO). We first formulate the near-field spatial non-stationary channel model which is characterized by the distance between the user and each antenna on uniform and modular curved arrays. By fixing the total number of antennas while varying the degree of curvature, we investigate a fair case where the horizontal arc length of the curved array is the same as the planar array. We explicitly unveil the non-trivial impact of array curvature on extending the near-field region for cell edges. Then, for arbitrary array geometries and arbitrary-field channels, we estimate the spatial-domain channel by tackling a compressed sensing problem with a learned regularizer. Without relying on specific codebooks, we propose a denoising autoencoder (AE)-aided approximated message passing (AMP) algorithm and provide the corresponding theoretical replica bound. Finally, based on the estimated channel, we propose an optimization algorithm to maximize the sum user rate for sub-connected XL-MIMO systems by jointly designing the array geometry and hybrid precoding in the downlink. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed AE-AMP algorithm can effectively estimate the spatial non-stationary near-field channels with robustness and generalities compared to several conventional and deep-learning-based benchmarks. The improvement of data rate by using modular curved arrays with the estimated channel is also validated.
item.dc:creator: Kangda Zhi, Yi Song, Tianyu Yang, Tuo Wu, Tengjiao Wang, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: L-FAME: Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation EEG Dataset and Benchmark
item.description: arXiv:2605.22893v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a novel Longitudinal Focused Attention Meditation Electroencephalography (L-FAME) dataset and an accompanying benchmark, designed to foster research into the neural effects of various meditation practices and the evolution of these effects over a six-week training period. The dataset includes baseline EEG recordings from 74 healthy college participants, of whom 44 completed the six-week intervention and returned for post-intervention recordings, along with psychological assessments. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three distinct meditation groups: two mantra-based techniques (SA-TA-NA-MA and Hare Krishna) and one Breath Focus practice. Leveraging this unique longitudinal and comparative dataset, we propose a benchmark suite comprising three distinct classification tasks: (1) cognitive state decoding to distinguish between resting and meditation states, (2) fine-grained classification of the specific meditation techniques, and (3) cross-session adaptation to evaluate model generalization across the longitudinal time gap. We provide comprehensive baseline results for these tasks utilizing a range of classical machine learning algorithms and deep learning architectures. The complete dataset, preprocessing pipelines, and benchmark evaluation code are being publicly released, offering a valuable resource and a standardized framework for the development and comparison of new analytical methods in computational meditation research and EEG-based machine learning. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/L-FAME-Dataset-Benchmark/L-FAME
item.dc:creator: Angqi Li, Ab Basit Rafi Syed, Hamzeh Alzweri, Taosheng Liu, Barry H. Cohen, Saiprasad Ravishankar

item.title: Spectrum Anomaly Detection in OFDMA Systems: Simulation Framework and Benchmark Dataset
item.description: arXiv:2606.02102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wireless connectivity underpins modern society and industry, enabling critical applications such as 5G ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) for industrial automation. However, the openness of the wireless medium exposes it to spectrum anomalies, including unintentional interference and malicious jamming, which threaten communication and sensing functionalities in 5G and emerging 6G networks. Despite its importance, spectrum anomaly detection research is hindered by a lack of publicly available datasets reflecting real-world scenarios. To address this, we present a benchmark dataset for spectrum anomaly detection in orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing access (OFDMA) systems, a core technology for 5G and beyond. The dataset includes spectrograms generated across a distributed network of sensing units, covering five distinct jammer types, from simple noise to advanced pilot-aware attacks. These anomalies are simulated in an industrial factory environment using a versatile open-source framework developed and published as part of this work, enabling extensibility to new scenarios and interference types. We provide baseline evaluations for supervised and unsupervised learning methods, demonstrating the challenges posed by different jammers and highlighting areas for further research. The dataset and framework support reproducible studies and serve as a foundation for advancing spectrum anomaly detection, with applications extending to network digital twins. By bridging the gap in open dataset availability, this work empowers the research community to validate and compare advanced detection methods for resilient next-generation wireless systems.
item.dc:creator: Anton Sch\"osser, Mohammadhadi Salehi, Sinuo Ma, Philipp Schulz, Gerhard Fettweis

item.title: Deep-Unfolded Accelerated Projected Gradient for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO
item.description: arXiv:2608.03237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates energy efficiency (EE) maximization for the downlink of cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output systems under quality-of-service and per-access point power constraints. We first derive closed-form gradient expressions of the objective function with respect to the power allocation coefficients, and then propose an accelerated projected gradient (APG) approach to solve this problem. To reduce the computational complexity and runtime of APG, we propose a deep-unfolded APG framework that maps iterative APG updates onto a finite number of neural network layers, where parameters such as step sizes and penalty coefficients are learned from data. The proposed approach produces power allocation solutions through a fixed number of gradient-based updates without the need for line search or manual parameter tuning. Numerical results show that the method achieves EE performance comparable to the iterative APG approach while requiring significantly lower computational cost, with up to a 30-fold reduction in floating-point operations under the considered system settings.
item.dc:creator: Phuong Nam Tran, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Hien Quoc Ngo, Markku Juntti

item.title: A Knowledge-Centric Communication For Autonomous Cislunar Networks
item.description: arXiv:2608.04817v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Future lunar infrastructure requires communication as a persistent service rather than a mission specific capability. Communication, digital twin, and artificial intelligence (AI) research have advanced autonomy independently while largely assuming that system state can eventually be reconciled with ground truth. Cislunar communication violates this assumption because propagation delay is fundamentally limited by the speed of light, visibility is governed by orbital geometry, and autonomous decisions often precede confirming observations. Here we introduce a knowledge-centric communication framework in which a digital twin continuously integrates delayed observations, communication physics, learned models, uncertainty quantification, and mission objectives into an evolving Operational Knowledge State. To quantify what is known, how uncertain it remains, and how current it is, we define two quantities over the fused Bayesian belief maintained for each communication link: \emph{Knowledge Entropy}, the differential entropy of the posterior belief, and \emph{Knowledge Freshness}, which generalizes Age of Information (AoI) from a single information stream to the temporal validity of the fused Operational Knowledge State. We prove that distributed knowledge fusion systematically improves operational knowledge by reducing uncertainty and demonstrate its importance for mission success through simulations and comparisons with flight data from the Longjiang-2 lunar micro-satellite.
item.dc:creator: Afan Ali, Daniel Benevides da Costa, Ali Arshad Nasir

item.title: Low-Complexity Near-Field Channel Estimation and Subcarrier-Cooperative Hybrid Precoding for Wideband XL-MIMO OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.14373v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses both accurate near-field channel acquisition and scalable precoding for wideband extremely large aperture MIMO (XL-MIMO) OFDM systems, with particular focus on reducing complexity. In the considered system, each MIMO multipath component is characterized by five continuous angle-distance-delay parameters, making conventional sparse recovery methods computationally infeasible while suffering from grid mismatch. We propose a decoupled off-grid channel estimation algorithm based on sequential sparse Bayesian learning (SBL). By exploiting the separable structure of the OFDM near-field atom, the five-dimensional joint search is replaced by a sequence of low-dimensional operations and active-set inference, avoiding multiplicative scaling with the per-dimension grid sizes. A continuous-domain Newton refinement is incorporated based on the exact marginal likelihood to mitigate the grid mismatch. Based on the estimated multipath parameters, we then develop a subcarrier-cooperative hybrid precoding framework for multiuser wideband transmission. A large-scale-matrix-inversion-free alternating optimization algorithm is established to maximize the sum user rate, together with a non-iterative low-complexity design that exploits the parameterized channel structure and provides an effective initialization. Simulation results demonstrate the accuracy of the estimation methods compared to several benchmarks and the effectiveness of the precoding algorithm based on estimated channel parameters.
item.dc:creator: Kangda Zhi, Tianyu Yang, Giuseppe Caire

item.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
item.description: arXiv:2610.15446v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.
item.dc:creator: Jinbing Jiang, Feng Shu, Jiangzhou Wang

item.title: Reconfigurable Antenna-Enhanced ISAC: A Unified Perspective on Electromagnetic Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2611.04125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables sensing and communication (S&C) functions to share time, frequency, and hardware resources, offering an efficient paradigm for next-generation wireless systems. However, conventional fixed-configuration antenna (FCA) architectures provide limited flexibility in adapting the physical electromagnetic (EM) response of the end-to-end wireless link. This article develops a unified EM-adaptation perspective on reconfigurable antenna (RA)-enhanced ISAC systems. We distinguish transceiver-side (TSc-side) and environment-side (Env-side) RA deployments and identify five fundamental EM reconfiguration dimensions: position, orientation, radiation pattern, polarization, and frequency response. Building on this framework, we examine how these dimensions customize communication channels, actively control target information mapping for sensing, and reshape the interplay between S&C, particularly by improving compatibility between S&C requirements under shared resources. Two case studies illustrate how TSc-side and Env-side EM reconfiguration can improve spatial selectivity and the achievable S&C performance tradeoff. Finally, we discuss several promising directions for advancing RA-enhanced ISAC systems, including fundamental performance limits, low-overhead black-box optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled semantic ISAC.
item.dc:creator: Peilan Wang, Lei Xie, Weidong Mei, Jun Fang, Yihong Su, Hongbin Li

item.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2410.02583v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.
